title: God feels silent… and you think it’s because you failed.
paragraphs: God feels silent… and you think it’s because you failed.

But what if the silence you’re afraid of…
is actually where He’s doing His deepest work?

What if heaven isn’t ignoring you—
but preparing you?
And you’ve been misreading the quiet all along.

You tried to fix yourself, clean yourself up, be “better”…
and the silence only grew louder.
So now the thoughts creep in—

“Maybe I’m too far gone.”
“Maybe God is disappointed.”
“Maybe this is punishment.”
And here’s the truth most people won’t say out loud:

You don’t just feel silence.
You feel shame inside the silence.
Like you’re sitting in a dark room with your own failure echoing back at you.

Some of us aren’t just waiting on God—
we’re hiding from Him.
Because we know what we did.

The secret sin.
The compromise.
The moment you chose your way over His.

Psalm 46:10 says,
“Be still, and know that I am God.”

Not “be perfect.”
Not “fix everything first.”
Not “earn your way back.”

Because in the stillness—
God exposes what noise has been hiding.
Some scholars interpret this verse not just as a command to be calm, but as a call to surrender control, to stop striving and recognize God’s sovereignty even when we don’t understand His timing.
And that’s where it gets uncomfortable.

No more noise to drown your guilt.
No more busyness to hide your condition.
Here’s the part that changes everything.
The silence is not where God abandons you.

It’s where He confronts you—
not to destroy you…
but to save you.
“My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?” — Matthew 27:46
That was the Son of God stepping into the full weight of human sin—your sin, my sin—and experiencing the silence of judgment we deserved.

So that your silence…
would never mean abandonment again.

2 Corinthians 5:21 says,
“God made Him who had no sin to be sin for us, so that in Him we might become the righteousness of God.”

Not self-improvement.
Not behavior management.
Not pretending you’re okay.
So when you sit in silence now—
You’re sitting in a place where grace is reaching for you.
It calls it out—and then offers redemption.
You can’t carry secret sin and expect peace in silence.
Because silence amplifies what you refuse to surrender.

1 John 1:9 says,
“If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.”
So what do you do with the silence?
You don’t fill it with distractions.
You bring the sin into the light.
You call it what it is.
You lay it at the feet of Jesus.
Because the same silence that once felt heavy…
So if you’re in a silent season right now—
Ask what He’s inviting you to release.
Ask where He’s calling you deeper.
“Jesus, I stop hiding. I bring You everything.”
Because He always responds to a surrendered heart.
Let this be your moment of turning.
